subject: Morning edition, Tuesday, Sep 29: President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen…
body:
*The day's most important news. Five minutes. No spin.*

### President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the war.

Iran had offered terms to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the route for about a fifth of the world's oil shipments, and end the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, now in its seventh month. Iran's foreign minister said Iran will wait for a formal U.S. response before abandoning ceasefire talks. Eight U.S. Marines were injured by an Iranian missile in the strait on Sept. 14.

**Impact 4/5.** Determines whether an active war involving the U.S. continues and whether a key global oil route reopens. [Just Security roundup](https://www.justsecurity.org/159075/early-edition-september-28-2026/)

### The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.2% on Sept. 28, its highest level in 19 years, and U.S. crude oil rose 4.2% to $96.31 a barrel after President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

All three major stock indexes closed lower: the S&P 500 fell 0.77% to 7,683.69, the Dow 0.67% and the Nasdaq 0.92%. Brent crude briefly traded above $108 before settling near $98. The 10-year yield is a benchmark for mortgage and other long-term loan rates.

**Impact 3/5.** A 19-year high in the 10-year yield pushes up mortgage and loan rates nationwide; oil prices feed directly into gas prices. [TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-sept-28-2026)

### President Trump announced at 2:00 p.m. that Mesabi Metallics, owned by India-based Essar Group, plans a $15 billion steel mill in eastern Iowa, using ore from its mine near Nashwauk, Minnesota.

The mill would use iron ore from Mesabi Metallics' new mine near Nashwauk on Minnesota's Iron Range, which opened this month; the mine has hired over 200 of a planned 350 workers. Mesabi Metallics is owned by India-based Essar Group. No construction start date or mill job count was given.

**Impact 3/5.** A $15 billion private investment in U.S. steel capacity. Rated 3 rather than higher because it is a plan, not yet under construction. [MPR News](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/09/28/ore-from-mesabi-metallics-mine-will-be-used-for-15-billion-steel-mill-planed-for-iowa)

### Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran is waiting for an official U.S. response before ending ceasefire talks; an Iranian official said Iran will not change its position on its nuclear program.

The statements followed the U.S. rejection of Iran's proposal. An Iranian army spokesman also said Iran's forces are prepared for renewed U.S. attacks.

**Impact 3/5.** Shows where ceasefire talks stand, but is a statement of position, not a decision or action. [Just Security roundup](https://www.justsecurity.org/159075/early-edition-september-28-2026/)

### SpaceX's Starship reached orbit for the first time on its 14th test flight Monday, deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites.

The ship completed about six orbits over roughly 10 hours before splashing down in the Pacific west of Chile; the Super Heavy booster splashed down in the Gulf shortly after launch. SpaceX changed the booster after ice buildup caused problems on the previous flight. NASA plans to use a modified Starship as the moon lander for its Artemis program.

**Impact 3/5.** A first for the largest rocket built and a step required before NASA's planned Artemis moon landings; still a test program. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/28/spacex-starship-orbital-flight)

---

**Also today**

- **Sports:** The MLB regular season ended Sunday with the 12-team playoff field set. The Wild Card Series start Tuesday, Sept. 29.
- **Tech & Space:** AMD agreed to buy World Labs, the AI startup founded by Stanford professor Fei-Fei Li, for $8.2 billion.

**Coming up**

- Sep 29: MLB Wild Card Series begin (best of three).
- Sep 30: Federal fiscal year ends; government stays funded through Dec. 11 under the stopgap law.
- Oct 2: September jobs report, 8:30 a.m. ET.

That's the news. Put the phone down and enjoy your day.
